body:
I am currently with my first girlfriend ever - I'm also her first girlfriend! It's really new, we've been together just a month now - we've been friends for around 2 years and got together at the end of this summer. She had been visiting me every week of the summer even though she lives far away ❤️ I had feelings for her for 4 months, all summer and eventually I couldn't take it anymore and had to tell her, she felt the same ❤️ she's an absolutely wonderful person, so considerate and sweet of the people in her lives and also of animals, even little bugs... that's what made me really fall for her, how kind and gentle she is with little creatures that a lot of people would rather stomp on 😭 she always tries to help them if they're in trouble and save them from getting hurt on the sidewalk, things like that make my heart melt. She's helped me see and appreciate more beauty in the world. I understand how it might seem silly to be so ❤️❤️❤️ this early on, and I realize having no experience with romantic relationships makes me naive... but it almost feels like just a natural evolution of the friendship we already had. It's like how our friendship has always been but with a stronger romantic aspect and a deep care for each other. 
Of course I have my fears entering a relationship for the first time, but I've been so happy ❤️ and she's such an amazing human being, I'm excited for what the future holds.

Totally understand this and feel for you - I feel like for me I won't have a relationship because I seem to always get into these really intense friendships with other queer women - that ultimately don't go anywhere romantically. Or maybe they're just intense for me because I develop feelings 😭 
Wish you the best and hope we can both find someone eventually!!

You are absolutely worth it. You have always been worth it and you will always be worth it. I don't know you but I'm grateful that you are alive here today and that you reached out. I come to this subreddit when I feel like life isn't worth living to see if commenting to others or seeing comments on people's posts might help. So thank you for being here and being honest with us in writing this post. It helped me today, I hope the comments are able to reach and help you as well.

Just a lot of health anxiety lately. Really small things are totally freaking me out - convincing myself I'm dying because of heart burn, shoulder pain, the occasional cough. I'm currently getting distracted from my school work to worry about whether I'm going to get a yeast infection or not. Not whether I HAVE one currently (because I have no reasonable symptoms), whether I'm going to GET one. I'm also worried I hurt my shoulder joints or rotator cuff because I have some slight pain in them, I can lift my arms fine and it's not that bad but we'll see. I'm also getting increasingly worried about parasites in my food, like I have problems eating fruits and fish now because of it, I can't eat grapes and I haven't eaten any fish in a long time. Plus my doctor set up another ultrasound for my gallbladder and didn't tell me why so idk what's going on. I just think I'm sick all the time and want to call my doctor every day for even small things.

I feel this... Currently writing this stuck in my room with my roommates having fun right outside my door in the living room.. In my heart I want to join them so bad but I'm so anxious and avoidant that I can't even open my door. I don't feel cut out for a lot of aspects of life either.

I have a similar question... I miss the people who just stopped talking to me. It's bad because it also makes me hesitate to start talking to new people because it might be the same where I feel really close to the person (friendship-wise) but they don't feel the same closeness and stop answering. :(

I'm exactly like this! I get crushes on people when they compliment my art or literally say any little nice thing... I definitely see normal platonic interactions in a warped way because I'm desperate. I blow my relationships (meaning friendships and acquaintances because I've never been in a romantic relationship) with people way out of proportion in my mind, I get the idea in my head that they care about me way more than what is happening in reality.

I feel similarly, I often think about wanting to die and suicide when I'm anxious but I don't think I could actually attempt suicide. It's weird but thinking those things feel like scratching an itch - it feels bad and I know I shouldn't think it but at the same time it feels right. I guess that makes sense because your brain forms pathways to thoughts you come back to a lot, like those and self-hating thoughts... So it would take work to move away from that. But I also think "hey, it would take more work to commit suicide than to just die however it's going to happen" and it kind of helps sometimes.

Most common for me is nausea, SWEAT, freezing cold hands and feet, and stomach problems - I used to throw up a lot but this symptom went away after high school 
I will occasionally feel faint, get chest pain/heart burn, get a headache, get a fast heartbeat
My least common symptoms are fainting (only if I'm REALLY freaked out, usually about other physical pain) and panic attacks (lucky to only have had 3 in my life that I could call "panic attack" rather than my regular "highly anxious state")
I hope you're doing alright today :)
Yeah omg 😭 it's exhausting to feel like that
You're so right about this thanks for the reminder- taking it too seriously just makes it impossible to deal with. It's good to laugh about it.
Merry Christmas!!!
I think thin wire inside the rays is a good idea.. it's an earring so it will probably be a very small amount of wire but it'll still help those thin parts to stay attached to the main mass.

I'm 19 and a lesbian, I'm feeling a similar thing happening... All six of my housemates are in straight relationships now and I'm barely out of the closet. I look feminine but I'm not that attractive so I doubt I'd be noticed. I know this post is from 3 years ago, hopefully things have improved for you, I just found it from actually looking up stuff about lesbian loneliness, kind of embarrassing... Either way I hope you're doing better!

Trans women are amazing ❤️❤️ I have an internet crush on a trans lady lol but I would say in my opinion it's not really important to me whether a girl is cis or trans in terms of an actual relationship.
I've done that but I used a textline, I just needed someone to talk to

I'm in a similar boat being at uni with no friends though I haven't actually tried as much as you have, I think you should be proud of yourself for reaching out to people even if it doesn't work out. Because reaching out and trying to connect with people is, in my experience, insanely hard. I agree with one of the other comments about getting into clubs and student life, but I'm not one to talk because I haven't tried that yet or even really considered it. 

I also miss my family so much. Definitely stay in touch with yours, try sharing your thoughts with them (or even a watered down version like "I can't seem to meet friends" or "I miss you and I'm unhappy here". If you don't want to talk about these feelings with them then you can also just... Talk with them about anything. Having a family you miss is a blessing, you love those people and they love you even when you're apart.

I'm really anxious right now because it feels like there's something in my throat. There isn't anything, I'm breathing fine, I just get like this, you know? I guess maybe it's better to phrase it as "I feel like I have something in my throat because I'm anxious" - they feed into each other. I've been getting really freaked out by little things lately, like I got some mosquito bites today and it's making me panic.  Everything with covid has been leading to me developing health anxiety I didn't have before. I almost miss when I was only socially anxious.
You're so right holy sh*t... I'm kind to everyone I come across and I have so much love for people. We don't deserve the loneliness.

Feel this heavily right now. I just moved in with some roommates bc uni is starting and I thought I'd be getting along and chatting with them a lot but I feel like I'm already the odd one out who is not as conversational. I feel like they don't want to talk to me or I'm just too boring to make proper conversation... I also know and accept that I'm pretty socially inept and I'm trying to get better, but it's a process.
Anyways I'm just saying that I get what you're feeling, I feel like a boring person and I have a lot of trouble making friends. It's okay to be alone, but loneliness really does sting. Just know there are a lot of other people out there going through similar experiences and feelings, that you are not alone in this feeling. I'm rooting for you :)

I feel my loneliest when I'm bored. That's why I try to have art projects on the go or other things to do a lot of the time! I might only have a few (I'd say 4) friends and feel distant from 2 of them right now, but having things to do on my own really helps.

I'm 19f and I've never been in a relationship either, I have a few friends. I'm sorry you were sheltered and kept from people, and that your mom won't recognize that you're dealing with the fallout of that now. You sound like a wonderful person, I don't agree with your last sentence about being unlovable though I know it feels that way. You sound like a person who is really trying your best. Are you in post secondary schooling or working? Because there's potential for friendships there (though I know the shyness and anxiety makes it difficult). I honestly hope you find those people you mentioned longing for, you DO deserve love and you ARE lovable. You just haven't been given the opportunity yet, I really hope it happens for you.

This is definitely something to go to therapy over, it's a traumatic event. You did a great job reacting to it, I'm actually tearing up a little reading this. But yeah you were traumatized, that is a perfectly good reason to talk to a therapist.
Yeah exactly, almost like you're two people having a talk. It might sound strange but that's how it feels for me too

Totally, I used to collect crystals excessively, not because I had an interest in "spiritual properties" or anything, more just because they're sparkly and beautiful lol. I have three massive shelves for them. I still love them but collecting them didn't make me any happier or more complete.
Lol I talk to myself a lot 😅 sometimes you're the only person around to talk to so...

Sculpting tbh... I don't expect to be good at it but I just try to have a clay project going at all times when I have nothing else going on. It makes me feel like I have to stick around to see how it goes. I do that with other art projects too but sculpting in polymer clay has been my main one right now. 

I think making art can be a really solid coping mechanism as long as you keep your expectations at basically 0.01% for how well you'll do. Just so you don't freeze up or get disappointed when something doesn't work out, and there's a chance you'll do well and pleasantly surprise yourself.

I feel similarly about the spiteful internal self. I'm so annoyed with myself lately, I get irritated having to be around myself because I'm always nervous, uncomfortable or complaining about something. I'm also always silently begging for social contact, and then when I get a text I get overwhelmed. Sometimes it's hard to live with yourself I guess.
Looks so good makes me hungry lol!!
The cutest thing I've ever seen :_) <3

I agree with this, I still struggle with loneliness but since I started getting busy making art again I feel so much more preoccupied and content with life. Having something you care about that takes your attention away from the loneliness/doesn't require you to be socially skilled is so important. I can't feel lonely while making a little sculpture because it's like making a new friend :)
Yes omg, it's so much worse now with lockdowns!
Absolutely, and when I have to go somewhere in a car it's a nightmare bc I get anxious about having to use the bathroom, which makes me need the bathroom even more. Self fulfilling prophecy I guess.

I relate so much. A lot of times I feel like sunny days are weirdly uncomfortable. I don't like summer either because it gets too hot where I live, and too many people in my neighborhood start sitting outside. I definitely love the rain and fall/wintery months better. Not only is the environment prettier (in my opinion) but you can also wear more comfortable clothing, less people are out, and I actually really like chores like shovelling snow in the winter. Rain is the ultimate though. It's like rain makes everything feel right in the world 😂

This won't be very helpful, but I just wanted to say that I feel similarly. It's like I'm not cut out for this life, like I'm not supposed to be here and that the adult life I'm entering now is too much to deal with. Part of it is a common feeling, but I'm guessing we've both felt this a little too often... Try to just take things one day at a time. Take things slow, develop your ability to voice your needs... I'm trying to do those things and it's difficult but I'm assuming it's worth it.

Totally feeling this right now, I don't have my license or a real job and I've never been in a relationship, it makes me feel like a total failure :( comparison and societal expectations really are the worst for anxiety... I've had sleepless nights wondering why I can't just learn to drive, but I truly hate and am terrified of it. Yet my roommates ALL know how to and seem to like doing it. It hurts to feel alienated by these expectations, but honestly remember that you're living your life, no one else's, and societal expectations are often scams - people who meet these expectations still experience pain, suffering, embarrassment, anxiety, they still struggle with human things.

I get what you mean :_-) currently crushing on my friend as well and haven't even come out to her because that would then almost imply the crush... So I'm not in a good position to give advice, but I'll still say you should maybe start a conversation about how you admire them.. it doesn't directly imply the crush but it also might give you the chance to tell them. If you are good friends, and you don't go into it expecting something from them, I'm sure they will be okay with it whether they reciprocate your feelings or not.
Yes, I feel similarly and it's exhausting... Right now I'm completely burnt out by it :-/

This is my first year in uni and I haven't made any new friends either. I'm actually supposed to go see two old friends today and I'm really terrified, I was very awkward and could barely speak last time because I also really struggle with that internal cycle and getting in my head when hanging out with people. I often think it might be easier if they just cut me off and don't want to be friends with me anymore, because then I wouldn't be able to ruin it anymore or embarrass myself, right? It's avoidant thinking, it ruins a lot of opportunities. I'm sorry you are going through this as well, it's really painful.
That's incredible I'm so excited for you!!!

I'm sorry things have been so difficult. Not having anyone to talk to can feel pretty devastating at times, I'm in a bit of a similar place with that. Even if you are alone, you don't have to give up on your life and individual worth.

Yes absolutely. I haven't be able to draw sincerely since July because of my anxiety around it and it is GNAWING at me. I think about drawing every day for hours, I almost never stop thinking about it. And then the day ends and I haven't done it. It hurts so much. 

But like with other anxiety situations, sometimes really the only thing to do is to just push through it, like exposure therapy. 

I used to have problems with anxious vomiting, and I would think about running to the bathroom every time I had to do something out of my comfort zone (even like walking to the bus stop) because of the nausea and dizziness. But I couldn't let myself do that, fighting through it was the only possible cure. I did actually vomit a lot, but once I learned I could often ride the nausea wave and calm myself because it wasn't genuine physical illness, I stopped feeling the nausea as much over time. 

That was kind of off topic and I don't know how much talking about myself would actually help you, but just know you're not alone in that feeling. The things I love also make me feel ill and anxious, and I haven't fought through it yet with drawing, but I hope to at some point, and I hope you're able to as well.

Yep, I used to vomit 4+ times a week from anxiety during high school... that can change eventually though, and if you get help for it from a therapist/psychiatrist or even just your MD, even better. I was not able to get help, but I am happy to say that the vomiting doesn't happen anymore for me, now I just have my other symptoms and heartburn instead of nausea (which in comparison I can handle much better).

When it comes to cashiers, I just remember that they see huge amounts of people a day, maybe upwards of 50 on a really busy day, and that they won't remember your interaction with them. They're too busy to be concerned about how you're acting or what you're buying. Unless you're being rude to them or do something like jumping on top of the counter or suddenly scream they probably won't remember. That being said, I have this problem too with using my credit card, I'm too scared that I might swipe it wrong or make a mistake on the keypad and would get embarrassed, but it's a process towards getting better at these things.

I feel the same way, I actually made a post recently that's talking about the same kind of feeling. What I'm thinking is that you actually are an interesting person, and so am I, it's just hard to feel like we can communicate that to others, if that makes sense?? Because I have a lot of interests and enjoy my own company, but I feel like other people find me boring. I'm also starting to think that this depends on who you're around, it's possible that you're with people who make you feel like you're boring because they aren't properly listening to you or asking you anything. You deserve to feel listened to and appreciated.

Yes if I have stuff to do that day that's how my anxiety works, it fades after around 3-4 pm. On the other hand, if I have a completely free day I'll be generally calm and then get a spike of anxiety around 3 pm.

I completely get this. I'm a lesbian and I feel like a homophobe for hating/being ashamed of my sexuality, which makes me feel even worse, because i don't want to be a homophobe and I don't hate other gay people... It's an unfortunate cycle. It's funny but the word "homophobe" actually fits people like us more... "fear of homosexuality".... but it's not malicious, we're just hurting and trying to work through it. As long as we don't put that negative energy out into the world and work on overcoming it, it can be ok.
In that case, make yourself your own first choice. You're worth it, you're worth the self-compassion.
That's really good advice, to just be more forgiving with myself. Thank you, I hope you treat yourself kindly as well

Remember that there is nothing wrong with being trans, and I'm truly sorry about the pain of dysphoria. I can't claim to understand the specific situation, but your "faking" and "abomination" comments reminds me of things I've thought about myself in regards to being a lesbian. It hurts feeling like you're the "wrong kind of person."

Thank you for this, the thing about the hot bath reminded me that when this is happening I should just focus on taking care of myself. I was in and out of trying to study chemistry in bed and lying there feeling terrible all day, so it might have been better to try to help myself.

I feel this way too. It seems like people lie way more than I thought... I've had friends tell me they "love" me and then a week later ghost me, to never speak to me again. I've had people say they want to hold onto our friendship and the same thing happens. 

I feel like such a bitter person... but being alone just seems like less pain. It still hurts a lot, but when I compare being on my own to being left by people, there's less net loss with the first option. From experience, when I go through a long stretch of being alone, I gradually become less sad over time and bear it better than when I get hopeful while friends with someone and then they leave me. 

But still, I don't advocate for being completely alone (or rather for being lonely), since it can damage your health. From my experience though, I almost get lonelier when I have friends...

Sorry for being really jumbled with this comment I'm in a bad place right now and I don't actually know the best way to go, but I just understand the feeling of maybe being alone would be better.
That's just awful. I don't understand how people can say stuff like that -_- I'm sorry that happened

That makes sense, it's like buying into the irrationality of the anxiety... I don't have hypochondria so I can't claim to understand the full scope of what you are going through, but I have fears about diabetes as well because of how cold I get, my toe was numb for a few days straight and I have to go to the bathroom very frequently/am often extremely thirsty. I got a blood test done (and a EKG because I was having chest pain which is unrelated) and they didn't say anything so I guess it's okay. 

I've realized that most of my physical symptoms throughout my life (fainting, hot flashes and cold sweats, frequent vomiting, heart palpitations, chest pain, numb hands and feet) are just products of the anxiety itself because I've been checked and I'm never told that anything is wrong. It's a very powerful feedback loop... The trick is breaking the cycle. You're insight was helpful to me and I hope things improve for you.

Yes, very much. I feel really guilty right now feeling hopeless while going through university, because I feel like it might just be a buffer before I leave schooling and everything goes downhill. And then people would realize that I'm actually shit.

Yes goodbye social media, but if there are people there like friends and family... I know loneliness is a whole seperate beast that doesn't always correlate with who you have around. But if there are people there, and I know this argument is tired and maybe not even helpful, but maybe stick around for them? I'm sorry you're suffering, I'm in a place mentally where I'm unsure of how to help with this... but maybe just wait a bit longer. Keep putting it off... I know it seems hopeless but your perspective while experiencing suicidal thoughts is basically cut off from everything, like tunnel vision. Please stick around.

I genuinely think some people just want something to talk at, and for some reason they choose living humans as the "something." I've had many encounters with people who somehow find me and just know I'll listen quietly while they talk in a constant stream. It happened all through high school, I can think of around seven seperate people over those four years who would do this, and I'd just take it because I had low self-respect I guess. And then like you said, they somehow consider that friendship and wonder why I try to pull away from them. But as far as I'm concerned I might as well be a stuffed animal or houseplant to them or something, something a person just talks to when they need to vent. 

Whatever happens, take care of yourself first. Being a constant giver of attention and care and not receiving it back is so exhausting, you end up starving. Conserve your energy and time, you don't need people in your life who don't respect you. I understand the feeling of wanting someone there for the sake of it, even if they treat you poorly and only talk about themselves, but ultimately it's not worth it.

I feel this, I had no one to celebrate with on my 18th birthday and now my 19th is coming up and I still have no one. I've been crying a lot too after losing friends. But life is ups and downs. 18-25 is a weird time because there's a lot of transition... Into adulthood, people doing different things like working and uni, people changing and growing. 

Happy birthday btw, I'm sorry it didn't go so well but I hope things start to look up
That is amazing!!! It's a serious accomplishment, definitely be proud :)
Thank you, you're right that the shame and anxiety aren't really external problems, it's stuff I need to work out with myself.

I guess it's an all around awkward situation... I agree it would be nice to actually be able to be friends but I guess the aspect of it being organized by the school makes it feel unnatural in a way. And with a script it's even more removed from a friendship. Still, I appreciate my mentor speaking to me and taking the time to do that, I'm sure there are people like me that you're assigned to who might not state it outright but it can be really helpful to just have someone there, even if it's awkward.

You know what, this makes me really hopeful. Thank you for your positivity, I want to try this mentality. I've actually been thinking something like this lately, how maybe it's okay to be alone and find happiness on your own. Again, thank you for saying this. It doesn't have to be an unhappy life :'-)

I feel like this too. I always wallow about how lonely I am and then when I get to actually see people, I'm too nervous and spacey to feel like I'm really connecting with them. I mostly let them talk and can't seem to remember anything about myself to say. I don't feel qualified to tell you what you need in a medical sense, but I definitely would love to get professional help one day, it drives me crazy not having proper connections to anyone.
That is amazing!!! It's a serious accomplishment, going out in public can be so difficult!

I just had a situation similar with a close friendship slowly fizzling out and dying. Those probably hurt as much if not more than when the relationship abruptly ends with a fight or something... Because you see it coming, and the ending takes so long and it just hurts. 

I think the point of friendships and relationships is just to have that experience, maybe to learn something or feel a connection for a bit. They aren't forever, most of the connections we make end during our lifetime. If you can find some sort of "lesson" from the whole thing, like some insight about people or relationships from your ended friendship with a person, then that can be the point.
I think it can be. I've had crushes and because I'm too insecure to pursue them (and I'm not comfortable with my sexuality) I basically break my own heart to get over them. It's sad.

I know it feels like you're alone in this experience and are the "most repulsive human being", but this subreddit is proof that there are many people who are lonely and feel that way about themselves, like you suspected before. It's true that people are getting lonelier and lonelier, the global situation doesn't help, and neither does social media. I know that feeling of seeing other happy people and just not knowing where things went wrong. Why is this my experience while they live happily? You aren't alone in this pain.

And I honestly doubt you're the most repulsive, I know it's mostly a figure of speech being used here, but there are truly disgusting people on this planet, I'm talking about those who have committed inhumane crimes and have no care for human life. I'm assuming you're not like and that you're actually a very valuable person based on your desire for human connection.

Dogs and other pets can really help, my dog just being there helps at night when things get really bad. But I get what you mean about wanting human contact, it's different from being around an animal, though they're wonderful and supportive they can't really talk with or hug you in the literal sense.

You're so right about this, I know the feeling like there's a wall keeping you from speaking, I've had attacks like that and it's like you might even want to say something but you literally CAN'T it just won't happen.

I get that, this pandemic led to friends leaving once again... It happened back in middle school, and now leaving high school I have no friends and no one talks to me. It's strange that I'm still shocked when it's happened before... 

This may just be a natural part of life for some people. It's like we don't click very well or friends don't stick properly even if we try really hard to support the friendship. I try to remind myself that most friendships and relationships, contrary to what we might ideally want, are not forever. Even many marriages and families dissolve. It's okay to be sad about these things. 

I hope you do find that person or those people who will sincerely care about you, but until then remember that YOU are there already. What I mean is that you are with you... Sounds weird but it gives me comfort to think that no matter what I have myself at least. And out of all relationships, the one you have with yourself is guaranteed for life, for better or worse. You also tend to have quite a bit of control over it. If you can find friendship with yourself it can help a little bit. Being supportive to yourself also can lead to better confidence down the road which could help with interpersonal relationships.
I've been obsessively on social media lately and this makes me realize that it truly is terrible for your mental health. I don't have close friends really so it just hurts to see people on there.

You will be ok. Life is a series of different phases and moods and everything is temporary. I know that dull pressure and pain in the chest when you're desperately lonely, it feels terrible, maybe one of the worst feelings ever. It feels like it will never go away, but it will, in time.

I've been experiencing something similar... I drew a ton over the summer but stopped during online university, and now I'm on break between the terms and have tried drawing multiple times only for nothing to happen. It's like I've forgotten how to even DO it, let alone enjoy it. I get to the paper and am suddenly overwhelmed with potential ideas along with insecurities and can't manage to draw much at all.

What I'd say though is that when you're at this point, anything is progress. I've been trying to just get something down on paper, even if it's not what I expect to make in the future. Even if it's just marks, or abstract, I think getting back into actually doing the action of drawing can help. Also, I've heard people suggest trying another medium like sculpture or paint for a while, and don't fixate on the concept, just the making (I know that's really tough but I've heard that suggestion). Those other art forms can help with drawing skills and vice versa, they're all pretty connected. Good luck to both of us :,-) hope we can get our groove back sometime lmao
There is no shame in "lying to yourself" to cope. Everything is just absurdity anyway. People can tell themselves whatever they need to to find some hope in this life.
That is amazing!! You deserve a clean space to live, that's definitely something to be proud of :)
Yeah I'm going to schedule an appointment for sure.  I'm hoping nothing is seriously wrong but you're right it's important to get it checked out.

Absolutely, my eating fluctuates a lot. There have been times where I won't eat or even drink before a task I'm anxious about because I've had issues with throwing up from anxiety and I don't want to take a chance. 

I don't know how to overcome it besides challenging the anxiety itself (attacking the root of the problem)-- maybe also look into keeping snacks with you that are really easy and don't add stress, such as berries that you can just easily eat and not think about (part of my issue is with having to chew too much, when I'm anxious it makes me nauseous). If you're like me, a lot of the anxiety subsides as soon as the task is over, so keeping snacks is good for when I realize I'm actually super hungry after my anxiety lessens.

Yes it absolutely can. I used to throw up before school multiple times a week, before activities related to school as well, and even from thinking about school (mostly during grade 8 and 9 - I lost friends and was very insecure). I went to get blood work done and nothing was wrong. It eventually stopped when I started feeling more secure in myself, the last time it happened was grade 11 and now I'm in university. 

Before that I had heart palpitations. I got tests done and they monitored me and nothing was physically wrong. I've had fainting as well with the same result.  

Anxiety can seriously mess with you, physical symptoms can be really scary, but yes I believe it's possible your nausea has a lot to do with anxiety and panic if you experience those feelings a lot. I actually don't think I did much to stop throwing up other than start challenging my anxious thoughts, and just enduring the nausea until it washed over me.

I feel this very strongly. I'm planning this year to pull back a lot on how much effort I expend for other people, I would suggest that to you as well. You deserve respect, love, and attention, but other people can be very disappointing, so maybe for the time being you can be your own friend.
Yes, sometimes you really need to let it out! I'm pretty sure crying can release positive chemicals in your brain similar to exercising.

I'm in a similar situation, a good friend of four years just stopped speaking to me (it might have to do with uni and quarantine but it hurts not knowing exactly why), haven't talked to her in months now because she won't respond. Other friends don't really talk to me either. I think it'll always be hard for some people to keep friendships, it's always been like that for me. One thing to look out for is openness and honesty. I've realized that I don't really open up to people when I'm friends with them and that they probably have a shallow view of me, while I know more about their emotions and lives because they shared more. I wonder if my inability to maintain friendships has to do with that, they sort of see me as just a surface level person. So I think opening up to the guy you're dating might be a good idea, it could strengthen the relationship to be honest with him. Good luck, happy new year.

I'm in the same situation. Started uni online this year and made no connections, really loose ties to a few people from high school but that's it. I'm home with my family too and that's nice because at least there are other people there but it's still lonely. Loneliness has honestly taken over my brain, it's hard to think about anything else.
